## Observation
In a sandboxed local `make verify` (worktree almondy-drop-acl-step, Nov 19 18:23 to Nov 20 01:14 PST, load average around 40), pytest-timeout (300 s, thread method) killed workers in `tests/unit/metrics/test_git_metrics.py::test_oracle_cap_change_events_compares_unsampled_adjacent_revisions` (inside `git_metrics._git` from `_py_blobs_at` / `module_size_trend`) and in 3 tests of `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_policy_dogfood.py` (inside the `_cli` subprocess helper). The same change passed CI Verified (Gerrit 3475).

## Root cause (verified)
Wall time is git starts times per-start latency, and these tests and the code under test start git once per revision and request. A counting git shim records 606 git starts for the oracle test: 182 from its own setup (60 x `add`, `commit`, `rev-parse`) and about 410 from `git_metrics` (per revision: `ls-tree` and `cat-file -p` for the cap file, `ls-tree -r` for modules; per sample: one `cat-file --batch`; all of it twice, once for `cap_change_events` and once for `module_size_trend`). A PATH git shim that sleeps 0.5 s before every start (606 x 0.5 s = 303 s) makes the test hit `+++ Timeout +++` every run. The same per-revision cost applies to `rebar metrics` on a long real history.

The dogfood tests do not share the defect: under the same 0.5 s shim (Nov 20 2026, origin/main) the whole module passes, slowest test 122.10 s call (`test_in_progress_to_open_resets_phase_and_requires_a_planning_review`), all others below that, so they fit the 300 s budget with no marker.

## Approach
- `src/rebar/metrics/git_metrics.py`: read every revision's cap in 2 processes instead of 2 per revision: one `git cat-file --batch-check=%(objectname) %(objecttype)` over `<sha>:.github/module-size-limit.txt` for all in-range commits (`missing` stays the ordinary not-qualified case, a non-blob stays `invalid`, a real git failure still raises and becomes `Unavailable`), then one `git cat-file --batch` for the distinct cap blobs. `module_size_trend` reads every sampled revision's blobs in one `--batch` instead of one per sample. A shared `_cat_file` helper and `_parse_batch_objects` parser serve both (`_parse_batch_output` keeps its counts contract on top of it). `_read_cap_at` is removed. Results are unchanged; `ls-tree -r` per qualified revision stays.
- `tests/unit/metrics/test_git_metrics.py`: the oracle test builds its 60-commit history with one `git fast-import` (helper `_fast_import_history`, shas from `--export-marks`) instead of 3 git starts per commit. Its assertions are unchanged.
- No config key, environment variable, flag or marker is added.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/metrics/git_metrics.py`
- `tests/unit/metrics/test_git_metrics.py`

## Testing
- Counting shim: the oracle test drops from 606 to 140 git starts (measured with the change).
- Under the 0.5 s-per-start shim the oracle test passes: 1 passed in 77.26 s (call 73.90 s), recorded here.
- All of `tests/unit/metrics` passes (178 passed, 2 skipped), including the existing missing-cap, invalid-cap and git-failure cases of `_qualified_history`.
- `make verify` through the verify slot.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Under the 0.5 s-per-start shim, test_oracle_cap_change_events completes inside the 300 s budget, with the shim run recorded here.
- [x] The plan-policy dogfood tests are measured under the same shim and either fit the budget or carry a justified `@pytest.mark.timeout(N)` per the pyproject policy.
- [x] `git_metrics` reads caps and sampled blobs in batches, with unchanged results on the existing metrics tests.
- [x] `make verify` passes and Gerrit gives Verified +1. (slot run 21626 + 226 passed; Gerrit 3499 LLM-Review +1, Verified +1; merged 863abe7cd19)
